thread:
maya: Quick follow-up on the precision-manifest RFC — we're seeing tail regressions on longctx when FP8 falls back to 4-bit. Any thoughts on interface boundaries for signaling a 'quality budget' to the runtime? cc @raj

raj: I saw that in the alerting dashboard. Do we have a minimized workload that reliably reproduces the drop? Would help to attach a short prompt + token distribution.

sam: Minimal repro I used: `Prompt: (legal contract summary) ~1024 tokens padded with random filler`. Observed: per-token logprob avg drops ~0.6 after the switch to 4-bit. Latency improves ~28% but quality delta is noisy.

maya: Thanks. High-level proposal: runtime should consume a per-model "precision manifest" that lists supported profiles and for each profile a `degradation_estimate` + `compat_flags` (kv_cache_compatible, softmax_rescale_hint, etc.). Then operators can set a global "quality budget" and runtime makes deterministic choices.

raj: Sounds reasonable. Thoughts on API shape? Two ideas: 1) manifest is internal only and Console exposes curated profiles, or 2) allow client hinting (header) like `X-Precision-Profile: prefer_fp8;fallback=int4`.

sam: I'm leaning internal-only for now. We shouldn't expose low-level knobs to customers until we have stable semantics. Maybe an internal header `x-rd-precision-hint` used by routing/edge for experiments, and user-facing Console switches map to vetted presets.

maya: Implementation notes: microbench command I used: `./bin/quant-bench --model redwood/v2-xl --profile fp8 --prompt test_longctx.json --warmup 50 --iters 200`. Canary should shadow low-bit path and compute a "degscore" per prompt.

ci-bot: Canary scheduled: 2026-04-02T02:00Z — will run 1k shadow requests across customer sample list (A/B). Results will be uploaded to /canaries/precision-manifest-2026-04-02.

raj: For fallback ordering we should keep two policy enums: `quality_first` (fp8->int8->4bit) and `latency_first` (int4 earlier). Add `fallback_policy` key in manifest and allow per-customer override for Dedicated.

sam: Telemetry needs: per-request `chosen_profile`, `degradation_score`, `kv_cache_version`, `prompt_hash`, and a small sketch of the prompt slice used for evaluation. We should log a stable manifest hash too.

maya: Important gotcha: KV cache compatibility across precisions. If `cache_compatibility=false` in manifest, runtime must invalidate the session cache when switching profiles (no silent hot-swap). That avoids subtle semantic drift.

raj: I'll sketch a minimal manifest example (proto):

```
{
  "model": "redwood/v2-xl",
  "manifest_version": "1",
  "profiles": [
    {"name":"fp8","degradation_estimate":"0.02","kv_cache_compatible":true,"fallback_order":["int8","int4"]},
    {"name":"int8","degradation_estimate":"0.08","kv_cache_compatible":true,"fallback_order":["int4"]},
    {"name":"int4","degradation_estimate":"0.25","kv_cache_compatible":false}
  ],
  "fallback_policy":"quality_first",
  "manifest_hash":"sha256:..."
}
```

sam: + add test matrix: 20 synthetic prompts covering factual, long-context, code, and safety. Unit check: degscore < 0.15 for quality_first when using fp8->int8 fallback.

maya: Action items: @raj prototype manifest schema + proof-of-concept runtime consumer; @sam build the microbench harness and the 20-prompt test suite; I'll draft the canary + eval rubric (AUC of degscore, stability window). Sync tomorrow @ 09:00 PT.

raj: On it. Also note: tie manifest to model version and require manifest_hash enforcement at deploy time so we don't run with stale manifests.

sam: 👍
